# Code Generation and Agent Repair Loop

This page covers what happens after you describe a task, attach a file, and approve what Auto-Mate may send. The AI agent writes a Python script for your task and writes its own tests for that script. It runs the tests, reads what failed, and repairs the script. Each test run is one attempt, and the agent gets a limited number of them: three by default. The tests run on **made-up data shaped like your file**, built from the column descriptions and sample rows you approved. **Your actual file is not opened at any point during this.**

Every attempt shows up in the conversation as it happens, and the code is one click away. The loop never pauses to ask whether it may try again. At the end, the agent chooses a final version of the script. Auto-Mate seals that version so it cannot change afterward.

In this build, the script stops there. It is not run on your real file, and there are no results to download yet. Checking the final version independently and running it are jobs for later features that are not built yet.

Three things to know before you rely on any of this:

- **Generated code runs without an isolation boundary in this milestone.** When the tests run, the Python the agent wrote runs with this application's own access to your computer. It can open other files on the computer that Auto-Mate itself can open, and nothing in this build stops it. The agent has no tool to read files, run commands, or use the network. That is a limit on the agent, not on the code it writes.
- **`uv run --no-sync --locked` does not restrict what the script can reach.** Those options stop `uv` from adding, removing, or updating packages when a test run starts, which prevents dependency drift. They do not limit which files, programs, or network addresses the script can reach.
- **Passing tests tell you about the code's shape. They do not prove it works on your file.** The tests ran on about 200 made-up rows. A script that passes them can still fail on row 40,000 of your real file, on a value the sample rows never showed, or on a column whose real contents differ from its description.

## What It Does

### From your request to a script

Code generation runs only for a task with at least one attached CSV, TSV, or XLSX file. A task without an attachment is a plain conversation: no code is written and no tests are run.

1. You describe the task, attach the file, and approve the review described in [Disclosure Review and Clarification](disclosure-review-clarification.md).
2. Auto-Mate checks that your approval still matches the file description, provider, and model. If it does not, the run stops before any test data is written or the AI is contacted.
3. Auto-Mate builds the made-up test data: one stand-in file for each attached file. It does this before it contacts the AI.
4. The agent receives your request, the approved file description, and a set of rules written by Auto-Mate. The rules say:
   - Write Python only. Use only Python's standard library and the installed packages. Do not install anything, do not use the network, and do not write shell scripts.
   - Read input files from the folder named in `AUTOMATE_INPUT_DIR`, using the exact file names given.
   - Write every output file into the folder named in `AUTOMATE_OUTPUT_DIR`, and list each one in a `manifest.json` there. A Plotly report must include the Plotly library in the file itself rather than load it from the internet.
   - Write pytest tests, then ask Auto-Mate to run them.
   - The test data is synthetic, so rely on the columns and types you were given, not on values you happened to see.
5. The agent writes the script and its tests through Auto-Mate's tools. Auto-Mate stores each file in its database and checks it first. A file name must be a relative `.py` path at most two folders deep. Test files must be named `test_<name>.py` or `<name>_test.py`. Each file must fit the size limit.
6. The agent asks Auto-Mate to run the tests, which uses one attempt. Auto-Mate freezes the current files as a numbered version and labels it with a fingerprint (a SHA-256 digest). It writes the files to `scripts/<run id>/attempt-<n>/` and runs pytest on the made-up data.
7. If the tests do not pass, Auto-Mate filters the test output with the same default-deny filter described on the disclosure page. Only the filtered text goes back to the agent. Each send is recorded as a "filtered diagnostics" receipt in the conversation. The agent then repairs the files and tries again.
8. When the tests pass, or no attempts remain, the agent picks a final version. It gives a plain-English summary, the input columns the script needs, and the outputs it will write. Auto-Mate records the final version even if that version's own tests failed.

While it works, the agent can still ask you a question, as described on the disclosure page.

### The made-up test data

For each attached file, Auto-Mate writes a stand-in file into `scripts/<run id>/fixtures/`. The stand-in is built only from the file description you approved, never from the file itself. A column or value that was left out of the approved description is also left out of the test data. The stand-in matches the real file in these ways:

- It has the same format and the same stored file name as your upload. A workbook keeps its sheet names and sheet order. A CSV keeps its delimiter, quote character, line ending, and text encoding. A script that opens the stand-in by name will therefore find your real file under the same name later.
- It starts with the header row, when your file has one. Next come the approved sample rows (up to 10), exactly as you saw them in the review. After those, invented rows fill the table up to 200 rows in total (`AUTOMATE_FIXTURE_ROW_COUNT`).
- Invented values follow each column's description:
  - Numbers stay inside the recorded minimum and maximum.
  - Dates stay inside the recorded range and use the detected date format.
  - True/false columns reuse the spelling seen in the sample rows.
  - Text is invented filler whose length falls inside the recorded range.
  - Empty cells appear at about the same rate as in your file.
- A column with few distinct values is filled with the frequent values that were already in the approved description, in proportion to how often they occur. A column with many distinct values never repeats one of its real sample values in an invented row.
- The data is repeatable. The same file in the same run always produces the same rows. A guidance retry is a new run, so it gets freshly invented rows, while the sample rows stay the same.

### What counts as an attempt

One request to run the tests is one attempt. Auto-Mate counts attempts in its own database; the limit does not depend on the AI keeping a promise. Each attempt ends in one of these ways:

| Result | Meaning | Counts as an attempt | Failure text sent to the agent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Passed | Every test passed. | Yes | No |
| Failed | The tests ran and at least one failed. | Yes | Yes, filtered |
| Could not start | pytest could not run the tests, for example because of an import or syntax error. | Yes | Yes, filtered |
| Timed out | The test run went past `AUTOMATE_TEST_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`. The test process and everything it started were stopped. | Yes | Yes, filtered |
| Stopped | The run was cancelled while the tests were running. | Yes | No |
| Not run | Auto-Mate refused the request and ran nothing. | No | No |

Auto-Mate refuses a test run for one of five reasons: every attempt has been used, the time limit is reached, the spending limit is reached, sending failure details was not approved, or `uv` or Python is not available. A refusal is recorded and shown in the conversation, and the agent is told to choose its final version. It is never a crash.

If you turned off **Allow filtered diagnostics for automatic repair** in the review, the first request to run tests is refused before anything runs. The run then ends as failed. Auto-Mate does not repair using failure details you did not agree to send.

### How a run ends

When the agent stops, Auto-Mate decides the result from what it recorded. It checks these conditions in order and uses the first one that applies:

| # | What happened | Run status | Code shown |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The time limit ran out, or the spending limit was reached after an AI turn. | Failed | `GENERATION_TIMEOUT` or `GENERATION_COST_LIMIT` |
| 2 | You selected **Cancel run**, or the server was shutting down. | Cancelled (`aborted`) | none |
| 3 | The AI provider failed during the run. | Failed | The provider's own error code |
| 4 | No attempt passed, and failure details were not approved. | Failed | `DISCLOSURE_SCOPE_NOT_GRANTED` |
| 5 | No attempt passed, and `uv` or Python was missing or the Python environment could not be prepared. | Failed | `PYTHON_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` |
| 6 | No attempt passed, and every allowed attempt was used. | Failed | `GENERATION_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED` |
| 7 | No attempt passed, and a test run was refused because of the time or spending limit. | Failed | `GENERATION_TIMEOUT` or `GENERATION_COST_LIMIT` |
| 8 | The agent chose a final version. | Completed | none |
| 9 | The agent stopped without choosing a final version. | Failed | `CODE_VERSION_NOT_FINAL` |

A **completed** run has a final version, and that version's own tests may have failed. For example, the agent may have finalized after a failing attempt while attempts were still left. Completed does not mean the script works on your file. Judging the final version is the job of the next feature, independent verification, which is not built yet.

A run that used every attempt without a pass counts as **failed**, even if the agent then chose a final version as it was told to. That version stays recorded and readable, marked as final with its tests not passed.

Two failures happen before the AI is contacted, so no attempts or summary line appear. The first is a file that cannot be turned into test data (`FIXTURE_GENERATION_FAILED`). The message names the file by its position, never by its name. The second is an approval that no longer matches (`DISCLOSURE_CONSENT_STALE` or `DISCLOSURE_CONSENT_REQUIRED`).

If the server restarts during a run, the run is not resumed. It fails with `EXECUTION_INTERRUPTED`, and every version and attempt recorded so far stays readable.

## How to Use It

### Follow a run in the conversation

Open the task after approving the review. The conversation fills in as the agent works:

- **Progress line.** While the run is active, a line at the bottom reads, for example, **Attempt 2 of 3 — repairing the script**. Other phases are **writing the script**, **running its tests**, **tests passed; choosing the final version**, and **no more test runs; choosing the final version**. A bar beside it shows how much of the time limit is used, such as **4 min of 10 min**. Time spent waiting for your answer to a question is not counted.
- **File writes.** Each `write_script` or `write_test` call shows its file path. In place of the file's text it shows a size, such as **wrote 4.1 KiB**. The code itself is kept in one place, the database, and is not copied into the conversation.
- **Attempt card.** Each tested version appears as a collapsed card, such as **Attempt 1 — 2 files, 84 lines**, with the first 12 characters of its fingerprint. Click it to load the code. The card lists every file with its line count and role. It shows each file as numbered plain text with a **Copy** button, and it shows **tests passed** or **tests failed**. There is no syntax coloring.
- **Diagnostics receipt.** When a test run fails, a line such as **Sent filtered diagnostics to anthropic `claude-sonnet-5` — 612 bytes** appears. Expand it to see exactly what was sent.
- **Test result.** A headline such as **Attempt 1: 1 of 3 tests failed.** appears with **2 of 3 attempts left.** under it. The filtered failure text the agent was shown follows in monospace. If the filter dropped lines, a plain sentence says so, for example: **14 lines of output were not recognized as safe to send, so they were dropped.** A refused request reads, for example, **Attempt 4 was not run because every allowed attempt had already been used.**
- **Test-data line.** Under every test result that ran, this line appears: **Tested against 200 synthetic rows built from your column descriptions and the 10 sample rows you approved. Your real file has not been read yet.** Select **Show the test data** to see the first 20 rows of each sheet, starting with your approved sample rows.
- **Final summary.** When the run ends, one line sums it up. For example: **Chose attempt 2 of 3 as the final version, which passed its own tests. Attempt 1: 1 of 3 tests failed. Attempt 2: all 3 tests passed.** A failed run also shows the **Run failed** panel with a plain-English message and its code.

If your browser disconnects, the run continues. Reopening the task replays the conversation, and the code, attempts, and test data are fetched again.

### When a run uses up its attempts

A failed code-generation run shows a panel headed **Tell me what I got wrong and I'll try again.** The panel lists what each attempt did. It has a **Your guidance (optional)** box that holds up to 2,000 characters, with a live counter. It has two buttons: **Try again** and **Not now**.

Selecting **Try again**:

- Starts a **new run** of the same task, linked to the failed one. The failed run is not changed and stays stored. The page switches to follow the new run.
- Reuses your approval and the answers you gave to pre-flight questions. You do not see the review screen again.
- Gives the new run its own full set of attempts, and freshly invented test rows (the sample rows stay the same).
- Adds your hint after your original request. The hint is sent to the AI provider as your own words, and it appears in the conversation as a second message from you.

The retry is refused in these cases:

- **The AI model, the provider, or the file description changed since you approved.** Your approval no longer matches, and the panel says so. Start the task again from **New task**, attaching the file again, and review what will be sent before approving. Auto-Mate does not reuse an approval that no longer matches.
- **You did not allow failure details.** The retry reuses that choice, so it stops at its first test run the same way. This build has no control to add the permission to an existing task. Start a new task and leave **Allow filtered diagnostics for automatic repair** on.
- **Another run is using the only active slot.** The limit is set by `AUTOMATE_MAX_CONCURRENT_EXECUTIONS`, which defaults to 1. Wait for that run to finish.

**Not now** leaves the run as it is. The panel appears only for a failed code-generation run. A cancelled or completed run shows no panel, although the API below accepts a retry of any finished run.

**What makes a good hint.** The agent has never seen your file. It knows the column descriptions, the approved sample rows, your request, and the filtered failure text. A useful hint fills the gaps:

- Name the columns that matter and what they hold. For example: "the amounts are in the Total column, and I want one row per month."
- Describe the result you want: which columns, how it is grouped, how it is sorted, and what the output file should be.
- Mention anything the sample rows would not show: day-first dates, a comma as the decimal mark, blank cells that mean zero, a totals row at the bottom, or rare values that need special handling.
- Use the attempt summaries. If the same column or step kept failing, say what that column really contains or what the step should do.
- Keep it short and specific. One or two concrete corrections work better than a restated request.
- Do not paste rows of your real data into the hint. Everything you type is sent to the AI provider as written, and it is not covered by the limits of the approved file description.

### Cancel a run

Select **Cancel run** while the run is active. Auto-Mate stops things in this order: a pending question, then Python environment preparation or a running test together with everything that test started, and then the AI session. A test cut short is shown as **stopped before the tests finished**, and the run ends as cancelled.

### Use the local API

The browser uses these routes, and you can call them directly on the local server:

```sh
# Every version of run 9, newest attempt first, without file contents.
curl http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/executions/9/code-versions

# One version with every file's contents and its declared inputs and outputs.
curl http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/code-versions/21

# Every attempt, the exact filtered failure text that was sent, and the limits.
curl http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/executions/9/attempts

# The made-up test data for run 9, with the first 20 rows of each sheet.
curl http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/executions/9/fixtures

# Start a new, linked run of a finished run, with guidance (optional, up to 2,000 characters).
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/executions/9/retry \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"guidance":"The amounts are in the Total column, and I want one row per month."}'
```

## Inputs and Outputs

### REST routes

| Method and path | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/executions/:id/code-versions` | A positive run id | `{ codeVersions }`, newest attempt first. Each entry has its id, attempt number, status, fingerprint, entrypoint, whether it is final, whether its tests passed, the agent's summary, and each file's path, role, size, line count, and SHA-256. No file contents. |
| `GET /api/code-versions/:id` | A positive version id | The same fields plus every file's `content`, `declaredInputs` (the files and columns the script says it needs), and `declaredOutputs` (the outputs it says it writes). |
| `GET /api/executions/:id/attempts` | A positive run id | `{ attempts, limits }`. Each attempt includes its status and refusal reason, its test counts and exit code, and whether a readable `manifest.json` appeared. It also includes the number of dropped lines, the duration, and `diagnostics`: the exact filtered text that was sent, or `null` if nothing was sent. `limits` holds `maxAttempts` and `timeoutMs`. |
| `GET /api/executions/:id/fixtures` | A positive run id | `{ fixtures }`. Each has the stored file name, format, sheet count, row count, sample-row count, byte size, SHA-256, seed, and a preview of up to 20 rows per sheet. The preview is rebuilt from the approved description and the recorded seed; no file is read. |
| `POST /api/executions/:id/retry` | Optional `{ "guidance": "..." }` of at most 2,000 characters. Blank guidance counts as none. | `201 { task, execution }` for the new, linked run. |

Values that appear in these responses:

- Version `status`:
  - `draft`: files are still being written.
  - `sealed`: frozen and not yet tested.
  - `tested_pass` or `tested_fail`: tested, with that result.
  - `superseded`: files were written but never tested before the run ended.
- Attempt `status`: `passed`, `failed`, `errored` (could not start), `timed_out`, `aborted` (stopped), `refused` (not run), or `running`.
- Refusal reasons:
  - `attempt_limit`
  - `time_limit`
  - `cost_limit`
  - `diagnostics_not_granted`
  - `runtime_unavailable`

No response contains a full path on your computer. Versions name files by their path inside the attempt folder, and test data is named by the stored file name only. The read routes need no special headers. The retry route applies the same browser-origin check as other state-changing routes. A `curl` request without an `Origin` header is accepted.

### Error codes

Errors use the standard envelope `{ error: { code, message, correlationId } }`.

| Code | Where you see it | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GENERATION_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED` | Run result | Every allowed attempt was used and none passed. The message reads like: "This run used all 3 attempts without getting the tests to pass. Tell me what went wrong and I'll try again." |
| `GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Run result | Writing and testing ran past `AUTOMATE_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS`. The message names the limit and the time used. |
| `GENERATION_COST_LIMIT` | Run result | The provider-reported spend reached `AUTOMATE_MAX_GENERATION_COST_USD`. The message names both amounts. |
| `CODE_VERSION_NOT_FINAL` | Run result | The agent stopped without choosing a final version. |
| `PYTHON_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` | Run result | The tests could not run because `uv` or Python 3.11 or newer was missing, or the Python environment could not be prepared. The message names both tools and gives the install command for each. |
| `DISCLOSURE_SCOPE_NOT_GRANTED` | Run result | The script could not be tested and repaired because sending filtered failure details was not approved for this task. |
| `FIXTURE_GENERATION_FAILED` | Run result | A file could not be turned into test data, for example because its analysis did not finish. The file is named by position ("File 1 …"). |
| `EXECUTION_INTERRUPTED` | Run result | The server restarted during the run. |
| `CODE_VERSION_NOT_FOUND` | HTTP 404 | No version has that id. |
| `EXECUTION_NOT_FOUND` | HTTP 404 | No run has that id. |
| `EXECUTION_NOT_RETRYABLE` | HTTP 409 | The run is still pending, generating, or waiting. Wait for it to finish or cancel it first. |
| `DISCLOSURE_CONSENT_STALE` | HTTP 409 on retry, or a run result | The file description, provider, or model no longer matches what you approved. |
| `DISCLOSURE_CONSENT_REQUIRED` | HTTP 409 on retry, or a run result | The task has no live approval. |
| `PREFLIGHT_DECISION_REQUIRED` | HTTP 409 on retry | A required pre-flight answer could not be carried over. |
| `EXECUTION_LIMIT_REACHED` | HTTP 409 on retry | Another run is using the only active slot. |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | HTTP 400 | A malformed id, or guidance that is not text or is longer than 2,000 characters. |
| `ORIGIN_REJECTED` | HTTP 403 on retry | The request came from a browser origin the server does not accept. |

Some codes are returned to the agent as tool errors so it can correct itself, and none of them ends a run on its own. `INVALID_CODE_PATH` means the file name broke the naming rules, and the message says what to change. `CODE_TOO_LARGE` means a file went over `AUTOMATE_MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES`. `CODE_VERSION_IMMUTABLE` protects a frozen version's files from being changed.

### Where files are stored

Auto-Mate adds these entries under its data folder:

```text
~/.automate/                        (or the folder in AUTOMATE_HOME)
├── env/                            shared Python environment for test runs
│   ├── pyproject.toml              written by Auto-Mate from the package list; do not edit
│   ├── uv.lock                     created by uv the first time the environment is prepared
│   └── .venv/                      managed by uv
└── scripts/<run id>/
    ├── fixtures/<stored file name> made-up test data; never your real file
    └── attempt-<n>/
        ├── main.py, test_main.py … the version's files, written from the database
        └── output/                 scratch space for that test run; nothing here is kept as a result
```

The database holds the authoritative copy of every generated file. The files under `scripts/` are written from the database for the test run. In this build, nothing cleans up `scripts/` folders, versions, or attempts on a schedule.

## Configuration and Permissions

Set these environment variables before starting the server. All seven are **provisional against open decision D14** (operational limits); the defaults may change when D14 is decided. A value outside the allowed range stops the server at startup with `CONFIGURATION_ERROR`, and the message names the variable.

| Variable | Default | Allowed values | What it limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTOMATE_MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS` | `3` | Whole number from 1 to 20 | Test runs per run, counted in the database. |
| `AUTOMATE_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS` | `600000` (10 minutes) | Whole number, 1 or more | Total time for writing and testing, counted from the moment the run starts. The clock pauses while the run waits for your answer to a question, and it resumes with the time that was left. When it runs out, a running test is stopped and the run fails. |
| `AUTOMATE_MAX_GENERATION_COST_USD` | `0` (off) | Number, 0 or more | Provider spend per run, in US dollars. It is checked after each AI turn and before each test run. |
| `AUTOMATE_TEST_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` | `120000` (2 minutes) | Whole number, 1 or more | One test run. When it runs out, the test process and everything it started are stopped. |
| `AUTOMATE_UV_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS` | `300000` (5 minutes) | Whole number, 1 or more | Preparing the shared Python environment. The first time, this downloads packages. |
| `AUTOMATE_FIXTURE_ROW_COUNT` | `200` | Whole number from 1 to 100,000 | Rows in each made-up table, including the approved sample rows. |
| `AUTOMATE_MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES` | `262144` (256 KiB) | Whole number from 1 to 16,777,216 | The size of one generated file. |

The spending limit is off by default on purpose. Auto-Mate counts only the cost your provider actually reports. With a provider that reports no cost, the limit could never trigger. Leaving it on by default would look like protection that is not there.

Some values are fixed rather than configurable:

- Guidance on a retry can be up to 2,000 characters.
- A generated file path can be up to 128 characters and two folders deep.
- The test-data preview shows up to 20 rows per sheet.

**Python packages.** Test runs can import the Python standard library and these pinned packages: `pandas`, `openpyxl`, `xlsxwriter`, `plotly`, `matplotlib`, `jinja2`, `python-dateutil`, and `pytest`. The list remains **provisional against open decision D05** (future dependency needs). The agent is told it may use only these packages and cannot install others. Auto-Mate copies its committed `uv.lock` to `env/` and uses `uv sync --locked` to prepare the environment. The first preparation needs network access to download the pinned interpreter and packages. Later test runs use `uv run --no-sync --locked`; those flags prevent dependency drift but do not restrict network access by the script.

**Prerequisites.** Test runs need `uv`; Auto-Mate asks it to install the pinned CPython 3.14.6 interpreter if it is missing. Without `uv` the application still starts, but runtime preparation fails with `PYTHON_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE`. To install uv on Windows, run `winget install astral-sh.uv`. On macOS or Linux, run `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`.

**Permissions.** This is a single-user local application with no accounts or roles. Anyone who can use it locally can read generated code, read the test data preview, and start a retry. A retry uses provider credit.

## Limitations

- **Generated code has no isolation boundary.** The test folder, the `uv` environment, and the removal of Auto-Mate's settings and credential-like variables from the test process tidy things up. None of them is an isolation boundary, and none of them stops generated code from reaching other files, programs, or the network. A restricted runner is required before the target-user pilot, and the technology for it has not been chosen.
- **Synthetic tests are limited evidence.** They cover the columns, types, ranges, and sample rows you approved, not the rows that were never described. A final version, even one that passed its own tests, has not been run on your real file.
- **No verification or real run yet.** Nothing checks the final version independently, runs it on your file, or turns its outputs into results you can open. Auto-Mate records whether a test run left a readable `manifest.json`, but that observation does not change any outcome.
- **One message covers every runtime problem.** A missing `uv`, a missing Python, and an environment that could not be prepared all end the run with the same `PYTHON_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` message. Preparation can fail when there is no network on first setup, or when it takes longer than `AUTOMATE_UV_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS`. The message does not say which of these happened. If both tools are installed, check the network connection and try again.
- **Retries have limits.** A retry cannot change your failure-details choice or pick up a new model. Both require a new task. The page offers a retry only for a failed code-generation run. After a server restart, the page suggests starting the task again, although the retry route also works for an interrupted run.
- **Only the latest run is on the page.** After a retry, the task page follows the newest run. The earlier run stays stored and readable through `GET /api/executions/:id/events` and the routes above, but this build has no history view for it.
- **Code is plain text.** The code view has no syntax coloring and no side-by-side comparison between attempts.
- **Nothing expires.** Generated code, attempts, and test data have no retention schedule in this build.
